messages.content: Write a Python worker that pulls items off a queue.Queue in a thread and processes each with a callback. Around 50 lines.

`thread_worker.py` in this repo already implements exactly this — `ThreadWorker` pulls items off a `queue.Queue` in a background thread and calls `callback` on each, with `put()`/`stop()`/`join()`, ~60 lines. Do you want me to reuse/import that, or do you specifically need a new standalone file (this repo already has five near-duplicate worker implementations: `worker.py`, `queue_worker.py`, `queue_thread_worker.py`, `simple_queue_worker.py`, `thread_worker.py`)?
Add a clean shutdown on a sentinel value.

`thread_worker.py` already has this — `_STOP` sentinel object (line 8), pushed onto the queue in `stop()` (line 40), and the worker loop returns cleanly when it sees it (lines 47-48), calling `task_done()` in the `finally` either way. Nothing to add here.
An exception in the callback currently kills the thread silently. Handle it.

This is already handled — `_run` (lines 43-53) wraps the callback in try/except, logs with `logger.exception` on failure, and still calls `task_done()` in `finally`, so one bad item doesn't kill the thread or leave the queue stuck. Nothing to change.
Add a maximum in-flight count so a slow callback cannot back everything up.

output: This already has it — `maxsize` at line 21/23 bounds the `queue.Queue`, so once that many items are queued, `put()` blocks until the callback drains one (line 17-18 doc it explicitly). That's already the max in-flight cap; a slow callback stalls producers rather than letting the backlog grow unbounded. Nothing to add.
